consensus_summary: All four blind responses identify tzitzit primarily as the divinely commanded tassels on garment corners serving as a visual reminder to remember and obey all of God's commandments and to live in covenant holiness, grounded chiefly in Numbers 15:37-41 and Deuteronomy 22:12. Common alternatives include the healing/messianic reading of Jesus' fringe (linked to Malachi 4:2 'wings'), the blue thread's heavenly/royal symbolism, and Pharisaic ostentation in Matthew 23:5.
book_summary: The book defines tzitzit as the tassels bound to the corners of the garment; looking upon them reminds the wearer of all the LORD's commandments, to do them. It cites Numbers 15:38-39 and cross-references a 'Wings' chapter.
consensus_core_identification: Tzitzit = corner tassels functioning as a mnemonic sign prompting remembrance of and obedience to God's commandments and covenant holiness.
book_core_identification: Tzitzit = corner tassels that, when looked upon, remind the wearer of all the LORD's commandments so as to do them.
boundary_disagreement: None. The book entry is a near-verbatim restatement of Numbers 15:39, which is exactly the consensus's primary meaning. The cross-reference to 'Wings' aligns with, rather than displaces, the common Malachi 4:2/garment-corner alternative noted in the consensus.
rationale: The book's core identification—tassels as a visual reminder to remember and do all the LORD's commandments—is essentially identical in referent, function, and extension to the consensus primary meaning stated by all four responses. The book adds no narrowing conditions and rejects no cases; the 'see Wings' pointer even anticipates the kanaph/wings typology the consensus lists as a common alternative. Differences are purely in brevity and wording.
strongest_objection: The book entry is terse and omits the holiness/consecration dimension (Num 15:40) that some consensus responses fold into the primary meaning; one could argue this is a slight narrowing to the mnemonic-obedience function alone. However, that dimension is an immaterial elaboration of the same core, not a boundary change.
